gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 12 build gate now carries both the existing virtio_scsi survey and the queue-layout plus recovery tests so this complex-driver lane stays reviewable without widening into runtime transport code.
The existing make target keeps the survey lane and the bounded driver test lane runnable in the same way as the other tranche checkpoints instead of hiding them behind ad hoc commands.

The Phase 10 virtio core slice already covers status sequencing, feature negotiation, queue callback bookkeeping, descriptor-shape metadata, and notification accounting, which is the minimum shared footing a future virtio_scsi starter depends on.

The existing virtio_ring helper keeps queue-shape and notification bookkeeping in memory only, which is the closest current Zigux surface for describing virtio_scsi control, event, request, and poll-queue topology without claiming DMA-backed queue execution.
A dedicated survey test still matters after the starter landed because it records the remaining roadmap gap around SCSI host lifecycle, TMF handling, event work, and DMA-backed request flow.

The lane needs a note that compares the landed queue planner, probe snapshot helper, restore queue rebind summary, event-buffer ownership summary, and rollback summary against the much larger virtio_scsi.c surface so future runs do not mistake this bounded foothold for a production SCSI HBA port.

The first honest virtio_scsi starter is now landed around an in-memory queue-family planner that models control, event, request, and request_poll virtqueue topology, preserves the Linux rule that poll queues must still leave one default request queue, and records a lab-only freeze or restore summary that blocks planning while transport is frozen and clears queue state after restore.

Dedicated driver tests now keep the starter honest around queue-count validation, poll-queue clamping, stable global virtqueue indexes, repeated transport-reset replanning across recovery generations, the bounded probe-config snapshot, and the bounded freeze or restore contract for planning and event recycling intent.

The slice note records exactly what the queue-layout, probe-config snapshot, and recovery starter covers so the survey can stay focused on the deeper transport, SCSI-host, and DMA-backed work that is still intentionally missing.

The first honest virtio_scsi probe follow-through is now landed as a bounded snapshot that records virtscsi_probe() config fields such as num_queues, seg_max, cmd_per_lun, max_target, max_lun, and max_sectors, plus the derived control or event versus request virtqueue layout before any blk-mq submission, TMF, or DMA-backed queue work is attempted.

The bounded recovery packet now records the virtscsi_restore() queue rebind order by naming the control and event queues, the default versus poll queue ranges, recreating request queues before device ready, and deferring event buffers until after device ready without claiming live DMA-backed submission.

The bounded recovery packet now also records restore-time event-buffer ownership by keeping the event queue reserved during freeze, preventing request queues from borrowing those buffers, and deferring event-buffer reuse until restore rearm after device ready.

The starter now also records one rollback-facing recovery summary that keeps the frozen queue layout available for restore, blocks queue planning and request access until restore, clears the live layout after restore, and requires replanning before queue reuse instead of pretending transport reset leaves request paths active.

Command submission, TMF and async notification handling, event-work scheduling, virtqueue buffer ownership, scsi_add_host(), scsi_scan_host(), blk-mq queue mapping, PM freeze or restore wiring, and DMA-backed request flow remain blocked even after the smaller probe snapshot helper because the roadmap-approved queueing and transport substrate is still not in place.
